services.name: Bare-root fruit trees
services.blurb: Peach, apricot, plum and almond in January and February, picked for valley chill hours.

services.name: Shade trees for valley summers
services.blurb: Pistache, valley oak and redbud that handle 105°F, sized to keep roots off the foundation.

services.name: Vegetable and herb starts
services.blurb: Tomatoes, peppers, squash and chiles in April, cool-season greens and garlic in fall.

services.name: Perennials and roses
services.blurb: Roses, lavender and salvias that bloom through the heat when watered deep and seldom.

services.name: Water-wise and native plants
services.blurb: Plants that keep a front yard looking cared for on two waterings a week.

services.name: Succulents and pots
services.blurb: Succulents and potted color for patios that sit in afternoon sun from June to September.

services.name: Soil, compost and mulch
services.blurb: Compost to loosen hardpan and mulch thick enough to keep July heat off the roots.

services.name: Delivery and planting
services.blurb: Trees delivered, set at the right depth, staked and watered in with a basin built around them.

services.name: Fruit tree pruning lessons
services.blurb: Winter Saturday sessions in the yard rows: where to cut so the tree fruits low enough to pick.

proof.label: Sample

reviews.text: My grandfather planted a Blenheim apricot behind this house in the sixties. When it finally died, Amparo found me the same variety bare-root in January and showed me where the old one stood too close to the fence.
reviews.name: Esteban M.

reviews.text: Our west wall bakes every afternoon. They talked us out of a sycamore, said the roots would find the slab, and sold us a Chinese pistache instead. Third summer now and the living room is noticeably cooler.
reviews.name: Paramjit S.

reviews.text: Come for tomato starts every April. They label which ones set fruit in the heat and which quit in July, which no other place bothers to tell you.
reviews.name: Dottie W.

reviews.text: Went to one of the winter pruning Saturdays with my two old peach trees in mind. Came home, cut them back the way they showed us, and picked fruit from the ground this summer instead of a ladder.
reviews.name: Harjeet K.

reviews.text: We pulled out half the front lawn. They laid out a list of plants that look decent on two waterings a week and delivered everything on one trip. Neighbors keep asking what the purple one is.
reviews.name: Vern C.

reviews.text: Busy on spring Saturdays, so go early. Still, someone walked the rose rows with me for ten minutes and wrote down which three would take the reflected heat off our driveway.
reviews.name: Lupe R.

reviews.text: Delivery crew planted a valley oak and a redbud, built a watering basin around each and showed my son how to fill it. Both made it through August with no leaf scorch.
reviews.name: Nadine B.

proof.guarantee: Bare-root trees that do not leaf out by May are replaced one time, no charge.
